svg.text: ESP32-CAM camera · Raspberry Pi 5 · any browser. Video travels over Wi-Fi: only power is wired.
One Wi-Fi network (2.4 GHz). A router, or the Pi as its own hotspot.
Pi pin 2 (5V), or its own 5 V supply
Power. Use 5 V, not 3V3: Wi-Fi current peaks brown out the 3.3 V pin.
Power return. Needed only when powering it from the Pi.
Flashing and the serial log, which prints the IP address.
Flashing only: hold low during reset, then remove for normal running.
Spoken prompts with --speak. The Pi 5 has no audio jack.
• A stable 5 V supply matters most: at least 1 A, 2 A preferred. Brownouts are the main cause of dropouts.
• The Pi 5's 5 V pin suits this with its 5 A power supply. A separate 5 V 2 A supply is the safer choice.
• Short, thick power wires: thin jumpers can drop enough voltage to reset the board.
• The ESP32 radio is 2.4 GHz only, so all devices must share a 2.4 GHz network or the Pi's hotspot.
• The ESP32 stream serves one client: the Pi. Browsers watch the Pi's /video, never the ESP32 directly.
• SerBot's control link is not written yet: the robot is simulated (robot/simulated.py) until a BaseRobot driver exists.
